item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q024_fibronectin_fragment_selection","answer":"d1uc6a1 and d1o5dt2 should both be treated as members of SCOPe family b.1.2.1, the fibronectin type III family, within superfamily b.1.2, fold b.1 immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich, class b all-beta proteins. The fragment annotation on d1o5dt2 means its classification supports homology only over the observed fibronectin type III core segment, not over missing residues or a complete domain architecture. In alignments, d1o5dt2 should be aligned only across the structurally present, overlapping beta-sandwich region; missing strands or loops should be treated as absent coverage, not as evolutionary insertions/deletions or evidence of unusual family diversity. For representative selection, a complete or better-covered domain such as d1uc6a1 is usually the safer representative, while d1o5dt2 may be useful only as a partial/template fragment for the region it contains. For interpretation, d1o5dt2 should not be used to expand the inferred sequence-length range, domain-boundary variability, functional repertoire, or structural diversity of the family without independent evidence from complete domains. Functional or template transfer from d1o5dt2 is correspondingly limited to conserved local features in the aligned fragment; absence of other features in d1o5dt2 is not evidence that those features are absent from the family.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
